record.notes: Introduced in the Senate on 1 May 2026; passed the Senate on 7 May 2026 (34-1) and the House on 9 May 2026 (57-6), and the Senate concurred in the House amendments on 12 May 2026. Approved on 14 May 2026 (Session Laws 2026, chapter 131). The act takes effect on 1 Jan 2027 and applies to consequential decisions made on or after that date; its rule-making provisions, a joinder clause and the appropriation took effect on passage. The Attorney General must adopt rules on post-adverse outcome disclosures and on the consumer rights to correction and human review by 1 Jan 2027, and may adopt rules clarifying 'materially influence'. The 60-day notice-and-cure provision is repealed on 1 Jan 2030, and annual enforcement reports begin in January 2028. The act creates no new private right of action and allocates fault between developers and deployers in discrimination actions by relative fault.

legal_force.quote: Be it enacted by the General Assembly of the State of Colorado:

summary.quote: In Colorado Revised Statutes, repeal and reenact, with amendments, part 17 of article 1 of title 6 as follows:

The act defines a 'consequential decision' as a decision that relates to an individual's access to, eligibility for, or compensation related to education, employment, housing, financial or lending services, insurance, health-care services, or essential government services and public benefits.
THE DEPLOYER SHALL PROVIDE A CLEAR AND CONSPICUOUS NOTICE TO A CONSUMER THAT THE DEPLOYER USED OR WILL USE A COVERED ADMT IN A CONSEQUENTIAL DECISION AFFECTING THE CONSUMER

THE DEPLOYER SHALL PROVIDE WITHIN THIRTY DAYS AFTER MAKING THE DECISION: (a) A PLAIN LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION OF THE CONSEQUENTIAL DECISION AND THE ROLE THE COVERED ADMT PLAYED IN THE CONSEQUENTIAL DECISION;
AN OPPORTUNITY FOR MEANINGFUL HUMAN REVIEW AND RECONSIDERATION OF THE CONSEQUENTIAL DECISION, TO THE EXTENT COMMERCIALLY REASONABLE.
IF THE DEVELOPER OR DEPLOYER FAILS TO CURE A VIOLATION WITHIN SIXTY
ON AND AFTER JANUARY 1, 2027, A DEVELOPER SHALL MAKE AVAILABLE TO EACH DEPLOYER OF A COVERED ADMT DEVELOPED BY THE DEVELOPER

judgment.status_reasoning: Approved 14 May 2026; section 5 (1): 'this act takes effect January 1, 2027', and section 5 (3): it applies to consequential decisions made on or after 1 Jan 2027. Only the rule-making provisions, a joinder clause and the appropriation took effect on passage. Today is 18 Oct 2026, before 1 Jan 2027, so the operative law is not yet in force: 'Adopted, not yet in force' stays.
judgment.scope_reasoning: AI-specific state law on automated decision-making technology in consequential decisions, replacing the Colorado AI Act; in scope with no note.
